mainTopic: Offering on a במה after the משכן; what items found at an idol are forbidden; an idol's property; and when an idol becomes forbidden.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא on ויקרא פרק יז. If an animal was made holy and also offered after במות became forbidden, the punishment is כרת, and the warning comes from 'פן תעלה עולתיך'. This fits רבי אבין's rule that 'השמר', 'פן' and 'אל' always mean a לא תעשה. If an animal was made holy while במות were allowed but offered after they were forbidden, there is a עשה and a לאו but no כרת. רבא then shows that 'ולא יזבחו עוד' can teach both this law and the idol-worship law learned earlier. Next a משנה rules that money, a garment or vessels found at an idol's head are permitted, but offering-type items are forbidden. The גמרא learns from two פסוקים that only decorative items are forbidden, and explains each permitted item as a case where it is not decorating the idol. It adds that inside an idol's partitions everything is forbidden, and that for פעור and מרקוליס even items outside the partitions are forbidden. A second משנה covers using an idol's garden or bathhouse, which אביי explains as depending on whether the כומרים profit. It also rules that a gentile's idol is forbidden immediately, which the גמרא shows follows רבי עקיבא against רבי ישמעאל. The amud ends as the גמרא starts explaining why 'places' in the פסוק must mean vessels, and that explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The first part of the verses: holy and offered while private altars were forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the first verses about slaughtering outside the משכן speak about קדשים that were made holy, and also offered, during the time when במות were forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Up to this point the verse is talking about holy animals that a person made holy at a time when private altars were forbidden, and also offered at a time when private altars were forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts dividing the פסוקים of ויקרא פרק יז into sections. This first section is about the 'simple' case, where everything happened after במות were forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two moments matter here: when the animal became holy (הקדש) and when it was offered (הקרבה). In this first case both happened during איסור הבמות, so the person is fully guilty.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals set aside as holy for קרבנות
Private altars outside the משכן or מקדש
The time period when private altars were forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two times. 'הקדישן' is when the animal became holy. 'הקריבן' is when it was actually offered. The ברייתא's whole split depends on these being two separate moments.

phrases.english: Up to here it is speaking
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the verses in ויקרא 17:3-4, about slaughtering outside and not bringing it to the אהל מועד.

phrases.english: about holy animals that one made holy
at a time when private altars were forbidden,
and offered them at a time when private altars were forbidden,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the ברייתא's reading of the verses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first section of ויקרא פרק יז deals with קדשים that were both made holy and offered during איסור הבמות.

steps.title: Proof: the verse gives a punishment
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves that the first section deals with a fully forbidden case, because the verse states a punishment for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: We know this because the punishment for it is stated, as it says: 'And to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting he did not bring it...' (and that man will be cut off).
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its reason for step 1: a punishment is written here, so this must be the fully guilty case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse ends with כרת. The Torah would only give such a harsh punishment where the person is fully guilty, which is when both the הקדש and the הקרבה happened in the forbidden period.

keyTerms.meaning: A punishment stated in the Torah
The entrance of the Tent of Meeting (the משכן)
'Etc.' — the rest of the verse continues

phrases.english: for their punishment is stated,
as it is said:
"And to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting
he did not bring it, etc."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:4. The end of that verse, which is not quoted here, gives the punishment of כרת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim of step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That the first section deals with הקדש and הקרבה both during איסור הבמות
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 17:4, which gives the punishment of כרת

steps.title: Where is the warning?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: we have the punishment, but where does the Torah give the actual prohibition?
steps.simpleTranslation: We have heard the punishment. Where do we learn the warning (the prohibition itself)?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא sets up the next move. It looks for the separate verse that actually forbids offering outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A punishment alone is not enough. The Torah needs to give a warning (אזהרה) that says 'do not do this' as well as the punishment. The verse in ויקרא gives only the punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: We have heard (we have a source for)

phrases.english: We have heard the punishment,
from where do we get the warning?
phrases.notes: An אזהרה is the verse that actually forbids the act, separate from the verse that punishes it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the warning that goes with the punishment found in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse source for the prohibition (אזהרה) against offering on a במה

steps.title: The warning: 'Lest you offer up your burnt-offerings'
steps.stepSummary: The warning comes from דברים: 'פן תעלה עולתיך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse teaches: 'Lest you offer up your burnt-offerings (in every place that you see).'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question by pointing to a verse in דברים that forbids offering קרבנות in any place you like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'פן' ('lest') in this verse is what makes it a prohibition. The next step explains why that word counts as a לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Lest' — a word that signals a prohibition

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"Lest you offer up your burnt-offerings."
phrases.notes: דברים 12:13

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The אזהרה comes from 'פן תעלה עולתיך' (דברים 12:13).

steps.title: The rule that 'השמר', 'פן' and 'אל' mean a prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this fits רבי אבין's rule in the name of רבי אילא: wherever the Torah says 'השמר', 'פן' or 'אל', it is a לא תעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This fits what רבי אבין said in the name of רבי אילא. For רבי אבין said that רבי אילא said: Every place it says 'beware', 'lest' or 'do not', it is nothing other than a negative commandment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps in to explain why the word 'פן' is enough to make a real prohibition. It brings a general rule from רבי אבין in the name of רבי אילא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this rule, someone might think 'פן' is only advice and not a real לאו. The rule tells us that 'השמר', 'פן' and 'אל' always create a לא תעשה, so 'פן תעלה עולתיך' really is the אזהרה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is used all over ש״ס to decide which verses count as real prohibitions.

phrases.english: And this is like what Rabbi Avin said in the name of Rabbi Ile'a,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי אִילָא:
phrases.english: for Rabbi Avin said that Rabbi Ile'a said:
Every place where it is said
"beware," "lest," or "do not" —
it is nothing other than a negative commandment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the verse from step 4 counts as a prohibition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The words 'השמר', 'פן' and 'אל' in the Torah always mean a לא תעשה.

steps.title: The second part of the verses: made holy while altars were allowed, offered after
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: the next section speaks about קדשים made holy while במות were allowed, but offered after they became forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here onward the verse is talking about holy animals that a person made holy at a time when private altars were allowed, and offered them at a time when private altars were forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves on to the second section of the פסוקים. This section covers a mixed case, where the two moments fall in different periods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the הקדש happened when במות were still allowed, so the person did nothing wrong when he set the animal aside. But he offered it after the איסור began, so the Torah still deals with it, as a different case from the first section.

keyTerms.meaning: The time period when private altars were allowed

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא splits ויקרא פרק יז into two cases. (1) Made holy and offered during איסור הבמות: there is כרת, and the אזהרה is 'פן תעלה'. (2) Made holy during היתר הבמות but offered during איסור הבמות: this is covered by the verses that follow.

phrases.english: From here onward it is speaking
phrases.notes: The next verse, ויקרא 17:5, about sacrifices that people were offering 'on the face of the field.'

phrases.english: about holy animals that one made holy
at a time when private altars were allowed,
and offered them at a time when private altars were forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא's division after the side discussion of the אזהרה, and gives the second section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The later section of ויקרא פרק יז deals with קדשים made holy during היתר הבמות and offered during איסור הבמות.

steps.title: The proof verse: offering on a private altar is like offering 'on the open field'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings a פסוק showing that offerings once allowed on במות must now come to the אהל מועד. Anyone who still uses a במה is treated like someone slaughtering in an open field.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the פסוק says: 'So that בני ישראל will bring their sacrifices which they slaughter.' These are the ones I already allowed you to bring on private altars. 'Upon the open field' teaches that anyone who slaughters on a במה when במות are forbidden is considered by the פסוק as if he slaughtered in an open field.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is giving the source for its last statement in step 6, about קדשים made holy when במות were allowed but offered after they were forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'which they slaughter' point to offerings that were already allowed on במות before the משכן. 'On the open field' tells us how the Torah sees a person who keeps doing this after the משכן is set up: as if he were offering out in a field, away from the proper place.

keyTerms.meaning: A private altar, used when it was allowed
A time when private altars are forbidden
The פסוק considers him as if

phrases.english: As it says: "So that the children of Israel will bring
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:5

phrases.english: their sacrifices which they slaughter"
which I already permitted you
phrases.notes: He means the offerings you were allowed to bring on private altars before the משכן.

phrases.english: "upon the open field"
teaches that anyone who slaughters on a private altar
at a time when private altars are forbidden
the verse considers him

phrases.aramaic: כְּאִילּוּ הוּא זוֹבֵחַ עַל פְּנֵי הַשָּׂדֶה.
phrases.english: as if he is slaughtering upon the open field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the case introduced in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: Offerings made holy when במות were allowed may not be brought on a במה once במות are forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 17:5 – 'אשר הם זובחים על פני השדה'

steps.title: There is a positive commandment, but where is the prohibition?
steps.stepSummary: 'והביאם לה׳' is a מצות עשה to bring these offerings to the משכן. The ברייתא asks where the לא תעשה is.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they shall bring them to ה'': this is a positive commandment. Where do we get a prohibition?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finds the positive command in the same פסוק and then asks for a negative command. It is setting up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Telling someone to bring the offering to the משכן is a מצות עשה. That alone does not make offering it outside a לאו, so the ברייתא looks for a separate prohibition.

phrases.english: "And they shall bring them to the Lord"
this is a positive commandment
and from where do we get a prohibition?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues reading the same פסוק and asks for the matching לאו.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for a לא תעשה against offering these קדשים outside the משכן.

steps.title: The prohibition: 'ולא יזבחו עוד'
steps.stepSummary: The לאו comes from 'And they shall not slaughter their sacrifices anymore.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And they shall no longer slaughter their sacrifices.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question by quoting ויקרא 17:7 as the prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads 'ולא יזבחו עוד' as a ban on offering on a private altar. This matters because elsewhere on the daf the same words are used for a different law, which רבא deals with in step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: And they shall no longer slaughter

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְלֹא יִזְבְּחוּ עוֹד אֶת זִבְחֵיהֶם״.
phrases.english: The verse states: "And they shall not slaughter their sacrifices anymore."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The לאו is 'ולא יזבחו עוד את זבחיהם'.

steps.title: Maybe the punishment is כרת?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises the idea that offering these קדשים outside might carry כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think he is punished with כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible mistaken idea so that it can reject it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that there is a עשה and a לאו, one might assume this is like other cases of offering outside the proper place, which carry כרת. The ברייתא checks whether that is true here.

phrases.english: Might he be punished with karet?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finding the עשה and לאו, asks how severe the punishment is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether offering these קדשים on a במה carries כרת.

steps.title: 'זאת להם': only this, not כרת
steps.stepSummary: From 'This shall be an eternal statute for them,' the ברייתא learns 'this' and nothing else: there is no כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'This shall be an eternal statute for them.' This applies to them, and not anything else.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that there is no כרת and brings its proof from the words 'זאת להם'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'זאת' (this) limits the law. These offerings get only what is written here, the עשה and the לאו, and not the extra punishment of כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: This applies to them, not another (punishment)

steps.whatToRemember: Offerings made holy when במות were allowed, but brought on a במה after they were forbidden: a עשה ('והביאם לה׳') and a לאו ('ולא יזבחו עוד'), but no כרת.

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״חֻקַּת עוֹלָם תִּהְיֶה זֹּאת לָהֶם״,
phrases.english: The verse states: "This shall be an eternal statute for them"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:7

phrases.english: this is for them, and not another for them.
phrases.notes: They get only the עשה and לאו written here, not the harsher punishment of כרת.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: חֻקַּת עוֹלָם תִּהְיֶה זֹּאת לָהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the idea in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No כרת, because 'זאת להם' means only this punishment and no other.

steps.title: רבא: read the פסוק two ways
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the words 'ולא יזבחו עוד' can be read two ways, so the פסוק teaches two different laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: read in it 'ולא יזבחו' (they shall not slaughter), and also read in it 'ולא עוד' (no more).
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא used 'ולא יזבחו עוד' for the ban on private altars. Earlier on the daf the same words were used for a different law, and רבא shows that the פסוק can carry both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One reading, 'ולא יזבחו,' gives the ban on offering on a במה. The other reading, 'ולא עוד' (no more to the שעירים), gives the law about idol worship that was learned from this פסוק earlier. So the ברייתא does not argue with that earlier teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: Read into it (read the פסוק this way)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how one פסוק can be read in more than one way so that two teachings fit together without a conflict.

phrases.english: Rava said: Read in it "and they shall not slaughter"
phrases.notes: This reading gives the ban on offering on a private altar.

phrases.english: and read in it "and no more."
phrases.notes: This reading gives the idol-worship law learned from this פסוק earlier on the daf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the apparent clash between the ברייתא's use of the פסוק and the earlier idol-worship use of it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא uses 'ולא יזבחו עוד' for במות, so the פסוק could not also teach the idol-worship law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק is read twice: 'ולא יזבחו' for במות and 'ולא עוד' for idol worship.

steps.title: The משנה: What You Find at the Idol's Head
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that money, a garment, or vessels found at the head of מרקוליס are permitted. Items like those offered on the מזבח are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone finds money, clothing, or vessels at the head of the idol, he may use them. But if he finds grape branches, grain wreaths, wine, oil, flour, or anything like what is offered on the altar, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sorts items found at the idol into two groups: permitted items and forbidden items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money, clothing, and vessels are not treated as part of the idol's worship, so they stay permitted. Items that look like altar offerings, such as grapes, wine, oil, and flour, are treated as offerings to the idol, so they are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Mercury, an idol worshipped by throwing stones at it
Vine branches heavy with grape clusters

keyTerms.term: כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ קָרֵב עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ
keyTerms.meaning: Something of the kind that is offered on the altar

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think everything left at the idol is forbidden. The משנה draws a line: ordinary useful items are permitted, and offering-type items are forbidden.

phrases.english: MISHNA: If one found at its head money
phrases.notes: 'Its head' means the head of the מרקוליס idol, which the earlier משנה was talking about.

phrases.english: a garment or vessels
these are permitted.
Branches of grape clusters,
and wreaths of grain stalks,
and wines, oils, and fine flour,
and any item the likes of which
is offered on the altar
is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins a new topic after the earlier discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money, garments, and vessels at the idol's head are permitted. Altar-type items are forbidden.

steps.title: What Is the Source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the משנה's rule comes from, especially that money, clothes, and vessels are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the משנה's ruling. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that some items near an idol are permitted needs a basis in the תורה. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
From where are these things learned?

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches which items found at an idol are permitted.

steps.title: Two פסוקים That Seem to Disagree
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר יוסף, quoting רבי אושעיא, cites two פסוקים. One lists wood, stone, silver, and gold 'with them.' The other mentions only silver and gold 'on them.' He asks how the two fit together.
steps.simpleTranslation: One פסוק says: 'You saw their idols, wood and stone, silver and gold, which are with them.' Another פסוק says: 'Do not covet the silver and gold on them.' How do these fit together?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אושעיא begins his answer by placing two פסוקים side by side and pointing out a gap between them. He is setting up his solution in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק seems to include everything near the idol, even plain wood and stone. The second פסוק names only silver and gold, which are decorations. The question 'הא כיצד' asks which פסוק sets the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: With them, meaning next to the idols
On them, meaning on the idols themselves

phrases.english: Rav Chiyya bar Yosef said
that Rabbi Oshaya said:
One verse says
"And you saw their abominations and their idols,
phrases.notes: דברים 29:16

phrases.aramaic: עֵץ וָאֶבֶן כֶּסֶף וְזָהָב אֲשֶׁר עִמָּהֶם״,
phrases.english: wood and stone, silver and gold, which are with them,"
and one verse says
"Do not covet the silver and gold on them."
phrases.notes: דברים 7:25

phrases.english: How so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question about the source by raising a tension between two פסוקים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source comes from comparing two פסוקים about items 'with' and 'on' idols.

steps.title: 'With Them' Is Read Like 'On Them'
steps.stepSummary: The answer: 'with them' should be read like 'on them.' Only decorative items are forbidden, and items that are not decorative are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'With them' is like 'on them.' On the idol, only decorations are forbidden. So too, near the idol, only decorations are forbidden, and plain items are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אושעיא solves the tension. The narrower פסוק ('on them') sets the rule for the broader one ('with them').
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'on them' mentions only silver and gold, the forbidden things are decorations of the idol. Applying that limit to 'with them' means only decorative items near the idol are forbidden. This explains why the משנה permits money, clothes, and vessels.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the key rule for items found near an idol: decoration is forbidden, and plain useful items are not.

phrases.english: "With them" is like "on them":
just as with "on them,"
a decorative item is forbidden
and what is not decorative is permitted,
so too with "with them,"
a decorative item is forbidden
and what is not decorative is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the tension between the two פסוקים raised in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading one פסוק in light of the other
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everything near the idol, even wood and stone, might be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only decorative items are forbidden, both on the idol and near it.

steps.title: Why Not Read It the Other Way?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reading: maybe 'on them' should be read like 'with them,' so that everything on the idol is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe say the opposite: 'on them' is like 'with them.' Near the idol, everything is forbidden, so on the idol too, everything is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי אושעיא's direction of comparison. Why should the narrow פסוק control the broad one, and not the other way around?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Comparing two פסוקים could go in either direction. If the broad פסוק ('with them', which includes wood and stone) sets the rule, then nothing is permitted. That would contradict the משנה, which permits money, clothes, and vessels.

phrases.english: But say: "on them" is like "with them":
just as with "with them,"
everything that is with them is forbidden,
so too with "on them,"
everything that is on them is forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the direction of the comparison made in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אושעיא's reading that 'with them' is limited by 'on them'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The comparison could just as easily go the other way, which would forbid everything.

steps.title: Otherwise 'On Them' Would Be Extra
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: if everything were forbidden, the תורה would not need to write 'on them' at all. So 'on them' must be teaching the limit to decorations.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the תורה should not have written 'on them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אושעיא's direction. The second פסוק only adds something if it sets a limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If everything near the idol is forbidden, things on the idol are surely forbidden too, so the פסוק 'on them' would teach nothing new. Since the תורה wrote it, it must be narrowing the rule to decorative items. This confirms the משנה's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: It should not be said, meaning the words would be extra

steps.whatToRemember: Near an idol, only decorative items are forbidden. 'On them' is read as a limit, because otherwise that פסוק would be extra. This is why the משנה permits money, clothes, and vessels.

phrases.english: If so,
let "on them" not be said.
phrases.notes: If everything near the idol were forbidden, things on it obviously would be too, so that פסוק would add nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17 and confirms the reading of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra-word argument: a פסוק must teach something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the broad פסוק sets the rule, so everything on the idol is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'On them' would be extra under that reading, so it must limit the prohibition to decorative items.

steps.title: Isn't money decorative?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: money is a decorative item, so how can money found on the idol be permitted?
steps.simpleTranslation: Money is a decorative thing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the משנה's ruling that money found on an idol is permitted. It points out that coins look like decoration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 set the rule that only decorative items are forbidden. Money can be used as decoration, for example coins hung up for show. So the משנה's permission for money seems to clash with that rule.

phrases.english: Money is a decorative item!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule from steps 16-18 (only decorations are forbidden) against the משנה's list of permitted items.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that money found on the idol is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Money is decorative, and decorations are forbidden, so money should be forbidden.

steps.title: Money in a purse tied around the idol's neck
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ינאי answer that the משנה means money in a purse hanging from the idol's neck, which is not decoration.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי say: it is talking about a purse that is tied and hung around the idol's neck.
steps.whatsHappening: The students of רבי ינאי answer the challenge. They say the משנה is talking about coins inside a closed purse hung on the idol, not coins shown off as decoration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Coins hidden inside a purse are not on display, so they are not decorating the idol. The purse is just a place to keep money. So the משנה's permission fits the rule that only decorations are forbidden.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai say:
It is speaking of a purse tied and hanging on its neck.
phrases.notes: "Its neck" means the idol's neck. The coins are inside the purse, so nobody sees them as decoration.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the משנה is about a specific case where the item is not decorative.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Money on an idol would be decoration and so forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Money closed up in a purse is not decoration, so it is permitted.

steps.title: Isn't a garment decorative?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה again: a garment is decorative, so how can it be permitted?
steps.simpleTranslation: A garment is a decorative thing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes the same kind of challenge, now about the garment in the משנה. Clothing on an idol looks like dressing it up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting clothes on an idol is a normal way to make it look beautiful. So by the rule from step 16, a garment should be forbidden. Yet the משנה permits it.

phrases.english: A garment is a decorative item!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 19, now aimed at the second item in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a garment found on the idol is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A garment adorns the idol, so it should be forbidden.

steps.title: A folded garment resting on the idol's head
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ינאי answer that the משנה means a folded garment placed on the idol's head, which is not decoration.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי say: it is talking about a garment that is folded up and set on the idol's head.
steps.whatsHappening: The same school answers again. A garment that is folded and just put down on the idol's head is not being worn, so it is not decoration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A garment decorates only when it is worn or draped for show. A folded garment is just being stored there. So it is not decoration, and the משנה can permit it.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai say:

phrases.aramaic: בִּכְסוּת מְקוּפֶּלֶת וּמוּנַּחַת לוֹ עַל רֹאשׁוֹ.
phrases.english: It is speaking of a garment folded and resting on its head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a non-decorative way the item was placed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A garment on an idol is clothing it, which is decoration.
steps.terutzMaskana: A folded garment just set down is not decoration, so it is permitted.

steps.title: Isn't a vessel decorative?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the third item: a vessel is decorative, so how can it be permitted?
steps.simpleTranslation: A vessel is a decorative thing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last item in the משנה, the vessel. A nice vessel set on an idol can also look like decoration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vessels can be placed on display to beautify something. So a vessel on an idol should count as decoration and be forbidden. But the משנה permits it.

phrases.english: A vessel is a decorative item!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as steps 19 and 21, now on the third item.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a vessel found on the idol is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A vessel can serve as decoration, so it should be forbidden.

steps.title: A pot turned upside down on the idol's head
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the משנה means a pot turned upside down on the idol's head, which is not decoration.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: it is talking about a pot that is turned over on the idol's head.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge about the vessel. A pot flipped over on the idol's head does not make it look nice, so it is not decoration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody decorates something by sticking an upside-down pot on its head. So it is not decoration, and the משנה can permit it.
steps.whatToRemember: All three items in the משנה (money, garment, vessel) are permitted only in a case where they are clearly not decorating the idol.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Where a pot is turned upside down on its head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23 and closes the series about the three items.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a non-decorative placement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A vessel on an idol is decoration.
steps.terutzMaskana: An upside-down pot is not decoration, so it is permitted.

steps.title: Inside the partitions everything is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי בר חייא rules: anything inside the idol's partitions is forbidden, even water and salt; outside, only decorations are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי בר חייא said: anything found inside the partitions around the idol is forbidden, even water and salt. Outside the partitions, a decorative item is forbidden, and a non-decorative item is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from רב אסי בר חייא. It splits the area around an idol into inside the partitions and outside the partitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside the inner partitions, we assume anything there was brought as an offering, so even simple things like water and salt are forbidden. Outside the partitions, the regular rule from before applies: only decorations are forbidden. This adds a location factor to the decoration rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Partitions or fences around an idol

steps.confusionAlert: Water and salt are not decorations at all, yet they are forbidden inside the partitions. Inside, the question is not decoration but whether it was brought as an offering.

phrases.english: Rav Asi bar Ḥiyya said:
Anything that is inside the partitions,
even water and salt, is forbidden.
Outside the partitions:
a decorative item is forbidden,
one that is not decorative is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new rule based on where the item is found, building on the decoration rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Inside the partitions, everything is forbidden; outside, only decorative items are forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the base for the next statement about פעור and מרקוליס.

steps.title: No partition rule for פעור and מרקוליס
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא reports a tradition that the partition rule does not apply to פעור or מרקוליס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: we have a tradition that there are no partitions for פעור or for מרקוליס.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר חנינא says the inside/outside split does not work the usual way for two special idols, פעור and מרקוליס. He does not yet say which way it changes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His words are unclear: does it mean everything is permitted, or everything is forbidden? This open question sets up the גמרא's next step.

keyTerms.meaning: We have a tradition; we hold
An idol worshipped by relieving oneself before it
An idol worshipped by throwing stones at it

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא: נָקְטִינַן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said: We have a tradition:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין קִלְקְלִין לֹא לִפְעוֹר וְלֹא לְמַרְקוּלִיס.
phrases.english: There are no partitions, neither for Peor nor for Mercury.
phrases.notes: The inside/outside partition rule from רב אסי בר חייא doesn't apply to these two idols.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא: נָקְטִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an exception to the partition rule of step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The partition rule does not apply to פעור and מרקוליס.

steps.title: What does 'no partitions' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical law follows from 'no partitions' for these idols.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי יוסי בר חנינא meant. This short question sets up the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'No partitions' could mean inside is treated like outside (more lenient) or outside is treated like inside (more strict). The גמרא wants to know which one.

keyTerms.meaning: For what? What does it mean in practice?

phrases.english: For what purpose?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the statement in step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'no partitions' makes the law more lenient or more strict for פעור and מרקוליס.

steps.title: It cannot mean inside is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests 'no partitions' means even inside is permitted, but rejects this: people offer even excrement to פעור, so surely they offer water and salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means even inside is like outside and permitted, that cannot be. People relieve themselves in front of פעור as worship. Would they not offer it water and salt?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the lenient reading and then throws it out. It proves that for פעור, water and salt can surely be offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lenient reading says water and salt inside the partitions would be permitted. But פעור is worshipped with something as lowly as excrement. So simple water and salt can certainly be offerings to it, and they cannot be permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion about to be rejected)
Relieving oneself, the way פעור is worshipped

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵימָא דַּאֲפִילּוּ פְּנִים כְּחוּץ דָּמֵי וְשָׁרֵי —
phrases.english: If you say that even inside is like outside and is permitted:
Now, they relieve themselves before it,
would they not offer water and salt to it?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא דַּאֲפִילּוּ פְּנִים כְּחוּץ דָּמֵי וְשָׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to step 27 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the lenient reading that inside the partitions is permitted for פעור and מרקוליס.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: פעור is worshipped with excrement, so water and salt are surely offerings to it and cannot be permitted.

steps.title: Even outside the partitions is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that for פעור and מרקוליס, even items outside the partitions are treated like inside and are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, even outside is like inside, and it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real meaning of רבי יוסי בר חנינא. For these idols, the whole area counts as inside, so everything found there is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, outside the partitions only decorations are forbidden. For פעור and מרקוליס that leniency is gone. Even non-decorative things found outside the partitions are forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: For most idols: inside the partitions everything is forbidden, outside only decorations. For פעור and מרקוליס: everything is forbidden, inside and outside.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, אֲפִילּוּ חוּץ כְּבִפְנִים דָּמֵי וְאָסוּר.
phrases.english: Rather, even outside is like inside, and it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אֲפִילּוּ חוּץ כְּבִפְנִים דָּמֵי וְאָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the lenient reading in step 28, gives the strict reading.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'No partitions' means the stricter rule: even outside the partitions everything is forbidden for פעור and מרקוליס.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For פעור and מרקוליס, any item found by the idol, even outside the partitions and even if not decorative, is forbidden.

steps.title: The idol's garden or bathhouse
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that you may use an idol's garden or bathhouse only if the use does not profit it. If others co-own it, you may use it even if it profits them.
steps.simpleTranslation: If an idol owns a garden or bathhouse, you may use it as long as your use does not profit the idol, but not if it does. If the idol and other people own it together, you may use it either way.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives the rule for property that belongs to an idol.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deciding question is whether your use brings the idol a benefit, such as a fee. When the idol owns the place alone, a profitable use is forbidden. When others are partners, the משנה allows even a profitable use.

keyTerms.meaning: 'To its advantage': in a way that profits the owner, such as paying a fee

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
An idol that had
a garden or a bathhouse:
one may benefit from them when it is not to its advantage,
but one may not benefit from them when it is to its advantage.
If it belonged to it and to others,
one may benefit from them both when it is to their advantage
and when it is not to their advantage.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁהָיָה לָהּ גִּינָּה אוֹ מֶרְחָץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins. It moves from the idol's partitions to property the idol owns.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Using an idol's garden or bathhouse is allowed only if the use does not profit the idol. If others co-own it, use is allowed either way.

steps.title: When a gentile's idol and a Jew's idol become forbidden
steps.stepSummary: A gentile's idol is forbidden as soon as it is made. A Jew's idol is forbidden only once it is actually worshipped.
steps.simpleTranslation: A gentile's idol becomes forbidden right away. A Jew's idol does not become forbidden until someone actually worships it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a separate rule about the moment an idol becomes forbidden to benefit from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a gentile, making the idol is enough to forbid it. For a Jew, making it alone does not forbid it; it becomes forbidden only once it is actually worshipped.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not reverse it. The gentile's idol is the one forbidden right away. The Jew's idol needs actual worship first.

phrases.english: A gentile's idol
is forbidden immediately,
phrases.notes: As soon as it is made to be an idol.

phrases.english: but a Jew's
is not forbidden until it is worshipped.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁל נׇכְרִי אֲסוּרָה מִיָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the last clause of the same משנה. It adds a separate rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gentile's idol is forbidden immediately. A Jew's idol is forbidden only after it is worshipped.

steps.title: אביי explains 'to its advantage' as profit for the priests
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that בטובה means profit for the idol's priests (כומרים). Profit that goes only to the idol's worshippers is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: 'To its advantage' means the priests get paid. 'Not to its advantage' means the priests do not get paid. If only the worshippers gain, it is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with אביי defining the word בטובה from the first clause of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה did not say whose profit counts. אביי says only payment to the כומרים, who serve the idol, makes the use forbidden. Profit that reaches ordinary worshippers does not forbid it.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Abaye said:
'To its advantage' means to the advantage of the priests,
'not to its advantage' means not to the advantage of the priests,
to exclude the advantage of its worshippers, which is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines a key word in the first clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Use is forbidden only when it profits the כומרים. Profit to the worshippers alone is permitted.

steps.title: A second version: אביי's words refer to the later clause
steps.stepSummary: Some teach אביי's explanation on the סיפא, the case of shared ownership. There, the משנה's 'to their advantage' means profit for the other owners, and 'not to their advantage' means no profit for the priests.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach it on the later clause: if the idol and others own the place, one may benefit whether it is to their advantage or not. אביי said: 'To their advantage' means profit for the other owners. 'Not to their advantage' means no profit for the priests.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of where אביי's statement belongs. In this version he is explaining the shared-ownership clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, אביי reads the permission in the shared case narrowly. You may pay, but only if the money goes to the other owners. If the כומרים get paid, it is still forbidden.

phrases.english: Some teach it on the later clause:
If it belonged to it and to others,
one may benefit from them whether to their advantage or not to their advantage.
Abaye said:
'To their advantage' means to the advantage of the others,
'not to their advantage' means not to the advantage of the priests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of אביי's statement and attaches it to the סיפא instead of the רישא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the shared-ownership case, use is allowed if it profits the other owners. It is forbidden if it profits the כומרים.

steps.title: The practical difference between the two versions
steps.stepSummary: If אביי was speaking about the סיפא, his rule applies all the more to the רישא. If he was speaking only about the רישא, then in the shared case even payment to the priests is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who teaches it on the later clause would certainly apply it to the first clause too. But the one who teaches it on the first clause holds that in the later clause, since others own it too, even profit to the priests is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares the two versions. It shows where they agree and where they give different rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions forbid paying the כומרים when the idol owns the place alone. They differ in the shared-ownership case. The second version still forbids paying the priests there. The first version allows it, because other owners are involved.
steps.whatToRemember: Both versions agree: if the idol owns the place alone, paying the כומרים is forbidden. They disagree only when others co-own it. One version forbids paying the priests even then; the other permits it.

phrases.english: The one who teaches it on the later clause
applies it all the more so to the first clause,
phrases.notes: If paying the priests is forbidden even when others share ownership, it is surely forbidden when the idol owns it alone.

phrases.english: but the one who teaches it on the first clause,
holds that regarding the later clause,
since there are others with it,
even to the advantage of the priests
is also permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּמַתְנֵי אַסֵּיפָא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן אַרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two versions from steps 32 and 33.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: When the idol is the only owner, paying the כומרים is forbidden in both versions. When others co-own the place, only the version that teaches אביי's words on the סיפא forbids it.

steps.title: Whose view is the rule that a gentile's idol is forbidden immediately?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that a נכרי's עבודה זרה is forbidden right away, and asks which תנא holds this view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: a gentile's idol is forbidden immediately. Whose opinion is the משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and asks which sage it follows. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא names the sage and brings a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 31 already stated this rule. Here the גמרא repeats the line for a new reason: to find out who holds it. That suggests some sages disagree about when an idol becomes forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is our משנה? (asking which sage it follows)
Forbidden immediately, as soon as it is made

phrases.aramaic: עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁל נׇכְרִי אֲסוּרָה מִיָּד.
phrases.english: A gentile's idol is forbidden immediately.
Whose view is our Mishnah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's rule from step 31 and asks who holds it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a gentile's idol is forbidden as soon as it is made?

steps.title: It is רבי עקיבא, based on a ברייתא about vessels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי עקיבא. It begins quoting a ברייתא that reads the פסוק 'destroy all the places' as speaking about vessels used for idol worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי עקיבא, as a ברייתא teaches: 'You shall surely destroy all the places where the nations served.' The verse is talking about vessels that were used for idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names רבי עקיבא and starts quoting the ברייתא that proves it. The proof itself comes a little later, when רבי עקיבא's view appears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא opens by saying the פסוק is really about vessels, even though it says 'places.' This opening is the shared starting point for the debate that follows. The גמרא comes back to it in step 39 to ask how 'places' can mean vessels.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Akiva, as it is taught:
"You shall surely destroy all the places
phrases.notes: דברים 12:2

phrases.english: where the nations served",
about vessels that were used for idol worship
the verse is speaking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 35 and begins bringing the source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי עקיבא, as the ברייתא below shows.

steps.title: Vessels are forbidden only once they are used, so רבי ישמעאל rules on gentile and Jewish idols
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from 'where the nations served' that vessels are forbidden only after they are used for worship. From this, רבי ישמעאל rules that a gentile's idol is forbidden only after it is worshipped, while a Jew's idol is forbidden immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think the vessels are forbidden even if they were made but not finished, finished but not brought, or brought but not used. So the verse says 'where the nations served': they are not forbidden until they are used. From here the sages said: a gentile's idol is not forbidden until it is worshipped, but a Jew's is forbidden immediately. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes through the steps of preparing a vessel for idol worship. It shows that none of these steps makes the vessel forbidden until it is actually used. Then it gives רבי ישמעאל's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'served' (עבדו) in the פסוק means past tense, actual use. So a gentile's vessel or idol becomes forbidden only once it is worshipped. A Jew's idol is stricter, according to רבי ישמעאל, and is forbidden as soon as it is made.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore the verse says (to teach otherwise)

steps.confusionAlert: This is NOT the view of our משנה. רבי ישמעאל says a gentile's idol waits until it is worshipped, but our משנה says it is forbidden right away. The proof for the משנה comes in the next line, from רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: You might think: if they made them but did not finish them,
finished them but did not bring them,
phrases.notes: Bring them, meaning bring them to the idol.

phrases.english: brought them but did not use them,
you might think they are forbidden?
So the verse says: "where the nations served,"
which teaches that they are not forbidden until they are used in worship;

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן אָמְרוּ: עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁל נׇכְרִי
phrases.english: from here they said: a gentile's idol
is not forbidden until it is worshipped,
but a Jew's is forbidden immediately,
these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and gives the first opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי ישמעאל, a gentile's idol is forbidden only once it is worshipped, and a Jew's idol is forbidden immediately.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא reverses the rule, matching our משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says the opposite: a gentile's idol is forbidden immediately, and a Jew's only once it is worshipped. This matches the משנה and proves the answer of step 36.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: it is the other way around. A gentile's idol is forbidden immediately, and a Jew's idol only once it is worshipped.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי עקיבא's view, which flips רבי ישמעאל's rule. This completes the proof that our משנה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says a gentile's idol is forbidden right away, and only רבי עקיבא says that. So the question of step 35 is now fully answered. For a Jew's idol, רבי עקיבא waits until it is worshipped. This matches step 31.

keyTerms.meaning: The matters are reversed, it is the other way around

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה follows רבי עקיבא. A gentile's idol is forbidden as soon as it is made, and a Jew's only once it is worshipped. רבי ישמעאל holds the reverse.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: the matters are reversed,

phrases.aramaic: עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁל נׇכְרִי אֲסוּרָה מִיָּד,
phrases.english: a gentile's idol is forbidden immediately,
and a Jew's only once it is worshipped.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite opinion, which is the one our משנה follows.
steps.raayaObject: That our משנה follows רבי עקיבא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא in which רבי עקיבא says a gentile's idol is forbidden immediately

steps.title: How can the verse be about vessels if it says 'places'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא's opening claim that the פסוק speaks about vessels, and challenges it: the פסוק says 'places.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: the verse is talking about vessels used for idol worship. But the verse says 'places'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the first line of the ברייתא and questions it. The פסוק says 'places,' so how can it be about vessels?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain words of the פסוק talk about the places where the nations worshipped, not about utensils. So the ברייתא's reading seems to go against the simple meaning, and the גמרא wants to know how it is justified.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written..., a challenge from the words of a פסוק

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא just quoted. The גמרא is going back to its first line.

phrases.aramaic: בְּכֵלִים שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּמְּשׁוּ בָּהֶן לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר.
phrases.english: The verse is speaking about vessels that were used for idol worship.
But "places" is written!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the opening line of the ברייתא (step 36) to examine it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that 'destroy all the places' is talking about vessels
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק explicitly says 'places,' so reading it as vessels seems to go against its plain words.

steps.title: Places themselves cannot become forbidden, since the mountains are not destroyed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer. The פסוק cannot really be about places, because the ground does not become forbidden. The פסוק itself shows this: 'their gods on the mountains,' not 'the mountains are their gods.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If it cannot apply to places, which do not become forbidden, as it is written 'their gods on the mountains,' and not 'the mountains that are their gods'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to explain why 'places' must be read as vessels. First it shows that places, meaning the ground, can never become forbidden. The second half of the answer, applying the teaching to vessels, comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the rule 'אם אינו ענין': if a teaching cannot apply to its own subject, we apply it to a different subject. The פסוק says to destroy 'their gods on the mountains.' That means the idols that sit on the mountains, not the mountains themselves, even if people worshipped them. Since the 'places' cannot be forbidden, the word must be teaching about something else, which is vessels.

keyTerms.meaning: If it does not apply to its own subject, apply it to another subject

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key principle for the rest of the סוגיא: something attached to the ground does not become forbidden through idol worship. Only movable things like vessels do.

phrases.english: If it is not relevant to places,
phrases.notes: This is the first half of a known rule: if it can't teach about places, use it to teach about something else. The second half comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: which do not become forbidden,
as it is written: "their gods upon the mountains,"
phrases.notes: דברים 12:2

phrases.english: and not "the mountains that are their gods,"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge of step 39.
steps.terutzResolutionType: אם אינו ענין: the teaching is moved from its own subject to another one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'places' should mean that the places themselves are forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Places attached to the ground never become forbidden, as the mountains show. So the word must be teaching about vessels. The גמרא completes this last part on the next amud.
